title: When the Confession Turns
premise: Dominic Sterling, the concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, has spent two decades cataloguing the town of Ashfall's secrets in a private ledger no one knows exists. When an elegant stranger named Iris Vane pays her a year's retainer to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the predicted killing of Ashfall's patriarch, Edmund Hale — Dominic dismisses it as theater until she finds the details of the prophecy matching entries in her own ledger from thirty years ago. As she investigates, Dominic discovers the 'prediction' is actually a confession: Iris is Edmund's illegitimate daughter, conceived during the summer three people conspired to steal the Hale inheritance and bury a man named Thomas Wren. The murder Iris fears is real — but the intended victim turns out to be Iris herself, and the would-be killer is the one person who loved Dominic enough to keep her invisible all these years: her late mentor, whose final letter reveals he staged everything to force Dominic out of hiding and into choosing love over duty. In the end, Dominic exposes the thirty-year-old crime, saves Iris, and burns the ledger — keeping only one page, the record of her own name.
about_author: Wren Coldharbour is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent eleven years listening to guests confess things they'd never tell their families. She writes mysteries about the people who overhear history rather than make it.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A woman in a gray coat pays Dominic a year's wages to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, naming victim, date, and method before leaving without a trace. Dominic's instinct says con; her ledger says otherwise. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Establishing chapter: Dominic's system of observation at the Grand Meridian, her rules (never involved, never remembered), and the ledger hidden behind the front desk. She checks the file on Edmund Hale and finds a page she doesn't remember writing. Beat: the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Edmund Hale Is Still Alive
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She visits Hale House under pretext of booking the estate for a hotel event. Edmund is sharp, cruel, and terrified of something he won't name. His son Julian watches her too closely. Beat: dread — the prediction feels less like fiction with every hour.

chapters.title: A Page Dated Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The anomalous ledger entry describes a drowning at Miller's Quarry, 1994 — written in her own hand, though she was nine years old. She begins pulling old newspapers. Beat: vertigo; the past is editing itself.

chapters.title: Iris Vane, Twice
chapters.summary: POV Iris. Flashback to Iris's childhood: her mother's deathbed story about Edmund Hale, a stolen inheritance, and a man called Thomas Wren who 'went into the water.' Beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Concierge Who Noticed Everything
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She interviews retired staff about the summer of 1994 and learns her own mentor, August Bell, took an unexplained month off that July. The town closes ranks around its oldest secret. Beat: betrayal's first taste.

chapters.title: Julian's Alibi
chapters.summary: POV Julian. Julian Hale rehearses his alibi for the predicted date — a charity gala, forty witnesses — while burning letters in his study. He knows more about Iris than he admits. Beat: guilt performing as confidence.

chapters.title: Miller's Quarry, Drained
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The quarry, drained for development, yields nothing but a rusted watch chain. But the developer's permit shows a signature: A. Bell. Beat: cold shock — her mentor's name in the mud.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic audits twenty years of entries and finds systematic gaps every July. Someone taught her to notice everything except one thing. Beat: the horror of realizing her invisibility was engineered.

chapters.title: Dinner at Hale House
chapters.summary: POV Iris. Iris infiltrates a dinner party as a caterer and comes face to face with Edmund, who recognizes her mother's eyes and drops a glass. Julian covers for her — why? Beat: dangerous tenderness between enemies.

chapters.title: The Confession Turns
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic confronts the aging police chief, who finally admits: Thomas Wren wasn't drowned by accident, and three people knew — Edmund, his late wife, and someone who signed a statement as 'A.B.' Beat: the title lands; the mystery becomes a cover-up.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Iris. Iris and Julian meet secretly; she came to destroy him and instead finds a man also held hostage by his father's crimes. She hesitates, and hesitation is a luxury the date won't allow. Beat: longing sharpened by countdown.

chapters.title: August Bell's Last Letter
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In Bell's sealed effects, Dominic finds a letter addressed to her, unsendable: 'You were the daughter I chose. Forgive what I did to keep you safe from what I did.' It confirms his role — and warns her to stop. Beat: heartbreak braided with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Date Approaches
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Three days out. Security at Hale House tightens; the chief refuses to act on a prediction; Iris has vanished from her hotel. Dominic realizes the prophecy's true target may not be Edmund. Beat: accelerating panic.

chapters.title: Who Pays in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Iris. Captured and questioned in the estate's east wing by someone who calls her 'the loose end,' Iris learns the retainer payment was traced — and that her employer's identity was never hers to hide. Beat: terror and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: The Night of the Prediction
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The gala proceeds; forty witnesses alibi Julian; and in the east wing, a second clock ticks toward midnight. Dominic abandons the desk — breaking her oldest rule — and crosses the lawn toward the house. Beat: duty inverted.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Blood
chapters.summary: POV Iris. Confrontation: Edmund confesses to the theft and the drowning, offering Iris the inheritance as absolution. She refuses it — and that refusal triggers the real killer, who cannot let any witness leave. Beat: power's corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: The Murder That Hadn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Climax part one: Dominic interrupts the attack meant for Iris, using twenty years of observed detail — the loose balustrade, the servant's passage — to turn the house against its predator. Beat: competence as catharsis.

chapters.title: The Killer's Name Was Always in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The attacker is revealed: the chief, protecting the 1994 pact, having manipulated Bell's letter and Iris's arrival to close the circle. Edmund dies of a heart mid-confession, taking half the truth with him. Beat: devastating cost.

chapters.title: Thomas Wren, Restless No More
chapters.summary: POV Iris. The quarry case reopens; remains are recovered and named. Iris claims her father's name, not his money, and leaves Julian standing in the rain with an apology neither can finish. Beat: mourning with dignity.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic feeds twenty years of other people's secrets to the lobby fireplace, page by page, keeping only the entry bearing her own name. The town breathes easier; she feels lighter and unmoored. Beat: release.

chapters.title: The Front Desk, Unattended
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, coda. Weeks later, Dominic and Iris share coffee in the empty lobby; a new guest approaches the desk where no one sits. Dominic lets them wait. Some secrets should find their own way home. Beat: quiet hope — visibility chosen at last.
